source_name: Македонска берза (Macedonian Stock Exchange) — Годишна конференција
why_relevant: The 24th annual MSE conference is a flagship MK finance event; agendas cover digitalisation, payment systems and fintech, with ~30 speakers from ~10 countries and bank/MBA participation. Speaker lists and sponsor pages are dated partnership signals.

source_name: Стопанска комора на Северна Македонија — настани (events calendar)
why_relevant: The national chamber runs a dense calendar of business/ICT/finance events, forums and B2B meetings; announcements typically list organisers, partners and speaking companies — a steady feed of vendor-to-bank contact opportunities in MK.

source_name: INFINTECH (Logate) — Western Balkans banking & fintech conference, Montenegro
source_subtype: regional conference — speakers, agenda, sponsor tiers
why_relevant: The main regional banking/fintech conference for the Western Balkans (400+ attendees, 30+ speakers; next edition announced for 8-9 Oct 2026). Dedicated /speakers/, /agenda/ and /become-a-sponsor/ pages make vendor spend and bank-executive attendance explicit; MK banks and vendors are in the catchment.

source_name: Balkan Payment Forum (ProMoney Events) — Tirana
source_subtype: regional payments forum — agenda & sponsor list
why_relevant: Regional C-level payments forum (200+ delegates from central banks, regulators, PSPs, fintechs across 20+ countries; 2026 edition 14 May, Tirana). Agenda themes are SEPA, cross-border and digitalisation — the exact procurement triggers for MK banks; delegate/speaker and sponsor lists surface who is selling into the region.

source_name: Money Motion (Zagreb) — largest CEE fintech conference
why_relevant: 2,000+ visitors from 600+ companies, 80-100 speakers; 2026 edition backed by Mastercard, NLB, Nexi, Erste, Erste Card Club, KeksPay, Raiffeisen Bank International and Robotiq.ai. NLB's group-level sponsorship is directly relevant to NLB Banka Skopje; the sponsor wall is a clean read on which vendors court SEE banks.

source_name: Balkan Fintech Association — regional events and members
why_relevant: Regional umbrella body whose event listings and membership roster point to Balkan fintech gatherings and to which MK players are affiliated; a snowball hub for events not indexed under 'North Macedonia'.

source_name: paytech.events — fintech/banking/payments conference calendar 2026-2027
why_relevant: Aggregated payments-event calendar useful for enumerating SEE/Balkan events by date and then jumping to each event's own sponsor/agenda page. Aggregator, so treat listings as leads not facts.

source_name: Macedonian e-Commerce Association LinkedIn page (and event posts by MK banks/vendors)
why_relevant: LinkedIn is where MK banks, PSPs and ICT vendors post 'we sponsored / we spoke at' content, usually with photos of the sponsor wall and named executives — often the only public record of smaller events and of which bank staff attended.

source_name: Комерцијална банка АД Скопје — awards & investor presentations (Global Finance, The Banker)
why_relevant: Bank self-reporting of international awards (Global Finance 'Best Bank in Macedonia 2025'; The Banker 'Bank of the Year' multiple times) is a dated recognition trail; presentations also list digital initiatives and partners behind them.

source_name: The Banker — Bank of the Year Awards (North Macedonia country award)
why_relevant: Annual country-level 'Bank of the Year' award for North Macedonia (Komercijalna banka nine times; NLB Banka reported twelve). Award write-ups often name the digital/core-banking projects that won it — i.e. vendor case studies with dates.

source_name: Global Finance — Best Bank Awards (North Macedonia) / EMEA Finance European Banking Awards
why_relevant: Two further international award programmes with MK country categories — Global Finance 'Best Bank in Macedonia 2025' (Komercijalna) and EMEA Finance Europe Banking Awards 2025 (double win reported for NLB Banka Skopje). Useful for tracking which bank is publicly claiming digital leadership each year.

source_name: ASEE / Payten (Asseco South Eastern Europe) — event and conference newsroom
why_relevant: The dominant regional banking/payments vendor group publishes which conferences it sponsors and speaks at (e.g. Money Motion coverage). A vendor-side mirror of the sponsor rosters, and a direct competitor-activity feed for the MK market.

source_name: Natech Banking Solutions — events & webinars (INFINTECH sponsorship disclosures)
why_relevant: Example of the vendor-side pattern worth systematising: core-banking vendors announce their sponsor tier at Balkan events (Natech = Bronze Sponsor, INFINTECH 2025). Vendor event pages often disclose sponsorship earlier and in more detail than the event site.

source_name: Германско-македонска конференција за контролинг (German-Macedonian Controlling Conference)
why_relevant: A recurring bilateral MK business conference with explicit thematic panels on banking and telecoms plus AI/digitalisation. Secondary for vendor rosters but useful for identifying bank CFO/controlling-side decision makers who appear on panels.

source_name: NBRSM international research conference series (SUERF co-hosted central banking conferences, Skopje)
source_subtype: central bank / academic conference (press coverage + programme)
why_relevant: The National Bank co-hosts international conferences in Skopje (e.g. with SUERF) on central banking, innovation and resilience. Programmes name senior regulators and international speakers — useful for regulatory-direction signals that precede bank IT spend.

source_name: Министерство за финансии на РСМ (Ministry of Finance) — official site
why_relevant: Owner of fiscal policy, fiscalisation legislation, e-invoicing mandate and the treasury; publishes strategies, draft laws, budget documents and press releases that set the payments/digitalisation roadmap and trigger procurement.

source_name: Архива на Министерство за финансии — стратешко планирање
why_relevant: Archive site holding older MoF strategic plans (2023-2025, 2024-2026, 2025-2027) that are no longer on the redesigned main site — needed for longitudinal tracking of digitalisation commitments.

source_name: Управа за јавни приходи (УЈП / Public Revenue Office) — official site
why_relevant: Regulator and operator of fiscalisation and the national e-Faktura platform; publishes fiscalisation forms (ФА-01 etc.), technical requirements, announcements and enforcement campaigns — directly determines which POS/fiscal-device vendors can operate.

source_name: УЈП е-Даноци / e-UJP taxpayer portals
why_relevant: Operational e-service front-ends for tax filing and payment; their launch notices, migration announcements and supported authentication/payment methods reveal the state's chosen technology stack and integration partners (e.g. digital ID, e-signature).

source_name: Царинска управа на РСМ (Customs Administration)
why_relevant: MoF body with its own e-payment/e-customs systems and IT procurement; a recurring buyer of payment and integration technology and a driver of state e-payment rails.

source_name: Електронски систем за јавни набавки (ЕСЈН / e-nabavki)
why_relevant: The single national e-procurement system: tender notices, awarded contracts and realised contracts for state bodies. The highest-value source for identifying which vendors win payments/fiscalisation/IT contracts with MoF, UJP, Customs, treasury and municipalities.

source_name: Министерство за дигитална трансформација (MDT) — Ministry of Digital Transformation
why_relevant: Successor to MIOA as owner of the national digital agenda: e-services portal, digital ID/wallet, open data, ICT strategy. Its strategies and key-activity pages define the e-government and digital-payment programmes that generate vendor selection.

source_name: Министерство за информатичко општество и администрација (МИОА) — legacy site
why_relevant: Predecessor institution; still hosts historical e-government, open data and ENER documentation that explains the origin of current digital-payment and e-service infrastructure and past vendor engagements.

source_name: Uslugi.gov.mk — национален портал за е-услуги
why_relevant: The national e-services catalogue; each service card lists payment information, competent body and legal basis — an operational map of where and how citizens pay the state electronically, and which services are digitised.

source_name: ЕНЕР — Единствен национален електронски регистар на прописи
why_relevant: Publishes draft laws and regulatory impact assessments BEFORE adoption, with public-consultation threads. Earliest possible warning of fiscalisation, e-invoicing, payment-services and ICT-strategy changes that will trigger procurement.

source_name: СМАРТ/МК: Дигитална Македонија 2030 (draft national digital strategy, June 2025)
why_relevant: The current-generation national digital strategy draft succeeding the 2023-2027 ICT strategy; expected to define digital-payment, digital-ID and e-government priorities to 2030 and therefore the medium-term procurement pipeline.

source_name: Национална ИКТ Стратегија 2023-2027 (MDT-hosted PDF)
why_relevant: Four-pillar national ICT strategy including digital government and business digitalisation — baseline document for judging whether current payment/fiscalisation programmes are on plan.
